theme: visual reasoning, Sanskrit anchors and semantic hypothesis construction
question: Can Bonta's recommendations and new Sanskrit comparisons supply preferred working meanings or functions across the remaining available sign inventory?
outcome: Catalogue covers 713 Wells codes: 117 inherited proposals and 596 new assignments. Sixteen new Sanskrit anchor families span seventeen codes; 256 additional two/three-sign windows involve 111 unknown codes. Preferred/alternative full-stem scenarios yield 164/158 nonempty full intersections, often with one context or several residuals. Priorities are 44 A, 230 B and 439 C. Three post-outcome lexical refinements concern heavy loads, collected provisions and share-bearing products. These are exploratory meanings, not authenticated readings.
challenge: 215 codes lacked a direct graphic-class mapping; source drawings have unresolved reuse rights; short dictionary residuals admit many completions; homonyms and later Sanskrit attestations complicate sense selection. Browser initialization timed out; worked-example selection and three drawing descriptions needed correction.
remedy: Inspected five additional local font sheets, retained every code and variant, selected explicit dictionary sense IDs, kept both anchor scenarios, and preserved successive catalogue projections and code copies. Independent recounts, 396 sampled lexical reconstructions, all window memberships and drawing links pass. Raw corpus strings, font drawings and full dictionary witnesses remain local-only.
retry_when: New registered artifact images, expert graphic concordances, longer independent strings or physical account/quantity associations can distinguish the retained semantic alternatives. Reuse this candidate map for those comparisons; do not treat dictionary construction support as independent validation.
